summary: Orca commits extensive engineering benchmarks: 139 tracked files under config/scripts/performance and 34 under tests/tools/benchmarks, plus committed raw artifacts (counterbalanced comparison.jsonl, benchmark.json and full-fold-benchmark.json with source hashes, and Windows startup/terminal result JSONs) that back specific before/after numbers (e.g. 81.513 -> 0.741 ms append scan, 19313 -> 2035.55 ms Windows startup on a 28k-file profile). The write-ups also report regressions and failures (+29.5% small-file cold scan, 104 ms vs 75 ms typing-latency budget). Reproducibility is limited: results are single-machine (Apple M4 Max or one Windows laptop), several documented commands point to old config/scripts/*.mjs paths that have since moved into config/scripts/performance/<area>/, and the computer-use benchmark (vs cua-driver) commits no results. The README's only figure is the tagline '100x builders', which is not a measurement.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
